title: Failed container startup loses the container needed for cleanup
reasoning: Container creation occurs before start, but self._container is assigned only after start succeeds. If startup fails, for example because a published host port is occupied, the created container remains in Docker while cleanup sees no container to remove. Repeated attempts accumulate orphaned containers.
reproduction: Make containers.create succeed and container.start raise an APIError, then call cleanup. The created container receives no removal request.
recommendation: Retain ownership immediately after creation and explicitly remove the container if startup fails, preserving the original startup error.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Container creation coverage exercises successful startup only; cleanup tests use runtimes without containers.
suggestedRegressionTest: Expand lifecycle coverage with startup failures after successful creation and assert removal, client closure, and safe repeated cleanup.
minimumFixScope: DockerStreamingRuntime container startup failure handling and lifecycle tests.
